title: Challenging adverse remarks in a confidential service report
p1:
A single negative remark in your service record can affect your entire career journey.

But can an employee challenge it, or is it permanently written in stone?
p2: Many people believe confidential service reports cannot be questioned because they are private documents. The surprising truth is that adverse remarks are not beyond review. Employees generally have a right to know about damaging remarks and may get an opportunity to represent their case.
p3:
A fair process matters. If a remark is vague, unsupported, or made without giving a chance to respond, an employee can seek review through the proper channel. The key is to act within the prescribed time and keep records of performance, achievements, and communications.

A confidential report should assess work, not become a tool for unfair punishment.
